questions.question: If the difference between the mode and median is 2, then find the difference between the median and mean (in the given order) using empirical relation.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mode - Median = 2

**Concept used:**

Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

**Calculation:**

Mode - Median = 2

⇒ Mode = 2 + Median ---(1)

We know that,

Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

From equation (1)

⇒ 2 + Median = 3(Median) - 2(Mean) 

⇒ 2 + 2(Mean) = 3(Median) - Median

⇒ 2 + 2(Mean) = 2(Median)

1 + Mean = Median

So, Median - Mean = 1

**∴ The difference between the median and mean (in the given order) using empirical relation is 1.**

questions.question: A lawn in the shape of a rectangle has an area of 7260 m² and its sides are in the ratio 5 : 3. Its perimeter is equal to the perimeter of a circular garden. What is the area of the circular garden? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of sides = 5 : 3 ⇒ Ratio area = 5 × 3 = 15 units².

15 units² = 7260 ⇒ 1 unit = √(7260 ÷ 15) = 22.

Rectangle Perimeter = 2 × (5 + 3) × 22 = 16 × 22 = 352 m.

Circle Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × r = 352 ⇒ r = 56 m.

Circular Area = (22/7) × 56 × 56 = 9856 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 9856 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

questions.question: In a circle, chords AB and CD are produced to meet at E. outside the circle. If AB = 9 cm and AE = 12 cm and ED = 4 cm, then what is the length of the chord CD?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the **External Secant Segment Theorem**, when two secants are drawn from an external point to a circle, the product of the length of one secant and its external part equals the product of the length of the other secant and its external part.

Logic: EA × EB = EC × ED

Given: EA = 12 cm, AB = 9 cm ⇒ EB = AE − AB = 12 − 9 = 3 cm

Also: ED = 4 cm, EC = ED + CD = 4 + CD

⇒ 12 × 3 = 4 × (4 + CD)

⇒ 36 = 16 + 4 × CD ⇒ 4 × CD = 20 ⇒ CD = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of secant segment **AE** = 12 cm

Length of chord **AB** = 9 cm

Length of external part **ED** = 4 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Intersecting Secants Theorem:** EA × EB = EC × ED

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/835c0f8a776f28edc0a546eab12a30bdc084b4afc1f3f3af724c00d0f3235fe7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ EB = AE − AB

⇒ EB = 12 − 9 = 3 cm

⇒ According to the theorem: EA × EB = EC × ED

⇒ 12 × 3 = EC × 4

⇒ 36 = EC × 4

⇒ EC = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm

⇒ We know that EC = ED + CD

⇒ 9 = 4 + CD

⇒ CD = 9 − 4 = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Internal Chord Theorem

If two chords AB and CD intersect inside a circle at point P, then PA × PB = PC × PD.

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent segment ET and a secant segment EAB are drawn from an external point E, then ET² = EA × EB.

Power of a Point

For a point E at distance d from the center of a circle with radius r, the value d² − r² is constant for any line through E and is equal to the product of the segments of any secant.</p

questions.question: A boat takes 7 hours to move 63 km downstream and 30 km upstream. The boat takes 6 hours to move 28 km downstream and 48 km upstream. How much time will it take to move 35 km downstream and 27 km upstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Downstream Speed** be D and **Upstream Speed** be U.

Equations: 63/D + 30/U = 7 and 28/D + 48/U = 6.

To eliminate U, multiply first equation by 8 and second by 5: (504/D + 240/U = 56) − (140/D + 240/U = 30).

364/D = 26 ⇒ D = 14 km/h; Then 63/14 + 30/U = 7 ⇒ 4.5 + 30/U = 7 ⇒ U = 12 km/h.

Required Time = 35/14 + 27/12 = 2.5 + 2.25 = 4.75 hours = 4 hr 45 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr 45 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Distance Downstream (d₁) = 63 km, Distance Upstream (u₁) = 30 km, Total Time (t₁) = 7 hr.

Case 2: Distance Downstream (d₂) = 28 km, Distance Upstream (u₂) = 48 km, Total Time (t₂) = 6 hr.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0afa425f6e39279ee622c9ee5ae4eb9f8e45615c6eb5f22cfcb9bf020373f0ce.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let 1/D = x and 1/U = y.

⇒ 63x + 30y = 7 --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ 28x + 48y = 6 --- (Eq. 2)

Multiply Eq. 1 by 8: 504x + 240y = 56

Multiply Eq. 2 by 5: 140x + 240y = 30

Subtracting the two equations:

⇒ 364x = 26

⇒ x = 26/364 = 1/14

⇒ **Downstream Speed (D) = 14 km/h**

Substitute x = 1/14 in Eq. 2:

⇒ 28(1/14) + 48y = 6

⇒ 2 + 48y = 6 ⇒ 48y = 4

⇒ y = 4/48 = 1/12

⇒ **Upstream Speed (U) = 12 km/h**

Time for 35 km downstream and 27 km upstream:

⇒ T = 35/D + 27/U

⇒ T = 35/14 + 27/12

⇒ T = 2.5 + 2.25 = 4.75 hr

⇒ 0.75 hr = 0.75 × 60 = 45 min

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr 45 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat and Stream

Speed of boat in **still water** = (D + U) ÷ 2 | Speed of **stream** = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Water

Downstream speed includes stream velocity helping the boat, while Upstream speed opposes it.

Average Speed for Round Trip

If distance is same both ways, Average Speed = (D × U) ÷ Speed in still water.</p

questions.question: If 75% of a number is added to 75, then the result is the number itself. The number is:

If 75% of a number is added to 75, then the result is the number itself.

**Calculation:**

Let the number be 100a

According to the question,

⇒ 75 = 100a - 75a

⇒ 75 = 25a

⇒ a = 75/25 = 3

So, the number = 100 × 3

⇒ 300

**∴ The number is 300.**

questions.question: A hundred rupee note measures 15 cm × 8 cm and a bundle of 125 such notes is 2 cm thick. Find the value of the hundred-rupee notes that can be contained in a box of size 48 cm × 36 cm × 30 cm, if the bundles are tightly packed in it without any empty space.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume of the box = 48 × 36 × 30 = 51840 cm³

Volume of 1 bundle = 15 × 8 × 2 = 240 cm³

Number of bundles = 51840 ÷ 240 = 216

Value per bundle = 125 × 100 = ₹12500

Total Value = 216 × 12500 = ₹27,00,000 = ₹27 Lakhs

**∴ The correct answer is ₹27 Lakhs.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dimensions of a 100-rupee note = 15 cm × 8 cm

Thickness of a bundle of 125 notes = 2 cm

Dimensions of the box = 48 cm × 36 cm × 30 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c7b41c92e324bf0900a5438c50125aa458e7ef4970655f65634f6521e369259.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

Number of items = Total Container Volume ÷ Volume of 1 item

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of the box = 48 × 36 × 30 = 51840 cm³

⇒ Volume of 1 bundle = 15 × 8 × 2 = 240 cm³

⇒ Number of bundles = 51840 ÷ 240 = 216

⇒ Total notes in the box = 216 × 125 = 27000 notes

⇒ Total value of the notes = 27000 × ₹100 = ₹27,00,000

⇒ Total value in Lakhs = ₹27 Lakhs

**∴ The correct answer is ₹27 Lakhs.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cuboid Volume

The space occupied by a 3-dimensional solid with rectangular faces is its volume, calculated strictly as Length × Breadth × Height.

Packaging Optimization

When checking how many small items perfectly fit into a larger container without any gaps, divide the total volume of the container by the volume of a single small unit.

Number System Units

In the Indian numbering system, 1 Lakh equals 1,00,000 (one hundred thousand). This conversion simplifies managing large monetary values in competitive exams.

questions.question: The ratio of the two numbers is 3 : 4 and their LCM is 480. Find their HCF.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **LCM** of two numbers is equal to the **product of their ratio terms** multiplied by their **HCF**.

Given **Ratio** = 3 : 4 and **LCM** = 480.

**HCF** = **LCM** ÷ (Product of ratio terms)

**HCF** = 480 ÷ (3 × 4) = 480 ÷ 12 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The **ratio** of two numbers = 3 : 4

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** = 480

**Formula Used:**

If the ratio of two numbers is a : b and their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is x, then the numbers are ax and bx.

The **LCM** of ax and bx = a × b × x

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9836cb95bebeb23103f7e3aaf988067a2cd5f829f90dcde13927d1cebe8cc8f7.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **HCF** of the two numbers be x.

⇒ The numbers are 3x and 4x.

⇒ **LCM** of (3x, 4x) = 3 × 4 × x = 12x

⇒ According to the question, 12x = 480

⇒ x = 480 ÷ 12

⇒ x = 40

Since x represents the **HCF**, the value of **HCF** is 40.

This matches the value given in **Option (2)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Two Numbers

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (n₁ × n₂ = HCF × LCM).

HCF of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are co-prime if their HCF is 1. Their LCM is always equal to their product.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

The HCF of a group of numbers is always a factor of their LCM.</p

questions.question:
If x = 2³ ​× 3² ​× 5 ​× 7³ ,y = 2² ​× 3³ ​× 5² ​× 7² , and z = 2⁴ ​× 3 ​× 5³ ​× 7 ,

then the HCF of x, y and z is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find the **HCF** of numbers in prime factor form, identify the **common prime bases** and select the **lowest power** of each.

Common prime bases are 2, 3, 5, and 7.

Minimum powers: 2², 3¹, 5¹, and 7¹.

HCF = 2² × 3¹ × 5¹ × 7¹ = 4 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 420.

**∴ The correct answer is 420.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = 2³ × 3² × 5¹ × 7³

y = 2² × 3³ × 5² × 7²

z = 2⁴ × 3¹ × 5³ × 7¹

**Formula:**

HCF = Product of the **lowest powers** of common prime factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a38652bb54e84583d47d6763444565cc9054fd139149cd253bf3f6f9373cb0bb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For prime 2: Lowest power is 2²

⇒ For prime 3: Lowest power is 3¹

⇒ For prime 5: Lowest power is 5¹

⇒ For prime 7: Lowest power is 7¹

⇒ HCF = 2² × 3¹ × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ HCF = 4 × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ HCF = 12 × 35 = 420

**∴ The correct answer is 420.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM of Prime Factorizations

To find the **LCM**, take the **highest power** of every prime factor that appears in any of the numbers.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, the product **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**.

HCF of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of **Numerators**) ÷ (LCM of **Denominators**).</p

questions.question: The average of 6 numbers is 16. If one of the numbers is excluded, the average becomes 17. Find the excluded number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Excluded Number = **Old Average** − (**Increase in Average** × **New Count of Numbers**)

Old Average = 16

Increase in Average = 17 − 16 = 1

New Count = 5

Excluded Number = 16 − (1 × 5) = 16 − 5 = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of initial observations (n₁) = 6

Average of initial observations (A₁) = 16

Number of observations after exclusion (n₂) = 5

Average after exclusion (A₂) = 17

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = **Average** × **Total Numbers**

Excluded Number = (Sum of 6 numbers) − (Sum of 5 numbers)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19778b27b6da6a70aba14d4bf1663a8834058f9feb606435641b56c95db43b8a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of 6 numbers = 6 × 16 = 96

⇒ Sum of 5 numbers = 5 × 17 = 85

⇒ Excluded number = 96 − 85

⇒ Excluded number = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

Average is defined as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Average = Σx / n.

Excluded Value Formula

When one value is excluded, the excluded value = (Old Average × Old Number of items) − (New Average × New Number of items).

Effect on Average

If the excluded number is **greater** than the original average, the average decreases. If it is **smaller**, the average increases.</p

Which two signs should be interchanged to make the equation correct?

12 × 3 ÷ 4 + 6 - 2 = 20
questions.solution:
**BODMAS Rule:-**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4cc639a088c2722789f521d8654dffcebce8723e33f056d46a41263cd3a2839.png] 

1. × and +

Given equation: 12 × 3 ÷ 4 + 6 - 2 = 20

After interchanging the signs, we get:

L.H.S = 12 + __**3 ÷ 4**__ × 6 - 2

= __**12 + 4.5**__ – 2

= __**16.5 – 2**__

= 14.5 ≠ R.H.S

2. ÷ and +

Given equation: 12 × 3 ÷ 4 + 6 - 2 = 20

After interchanging the signs, we get:

L.H.S = 12 × 3 +__** 4 ÷ 6**__ - 2

= __**36 + 0.67**__ – 2

=__** 36.67 – 2**__

= 34.67 ≠ R.H.S

3. + and –

Given equation: 12 × 3 ÷ 4 + 6 - 2 = 20

After interchanging the signs, we get:

L.H.S = 12 ×__** 3 ÷ 4**__ - 6 + 2

= __**9**__ – 6 __**+ 2**__

= __**11 – 6**__

= 5 ≠ R.H.S

4. × and ÷

Given equation: 12 × 3 ÷ 4 + 6 - 2 = 20

After interchanging the signs, we get:

L.H.S = __**12 ÷ 3**__ × 4 + 6 - 2

= __**16 + 6**__ – 2

= __**22 – 2**__

= 20 = R.H.S

Hence, ‘**× and ÷**’ is the correct answer.

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(1) from the statements

Statements:

a) Some sketch pens are ink pens

b) Some pencils are markers

c) All ink pens are markers

Conclusions:

I. Some markers are sketch pens

II. Some sketch pens are pencils

III. Some markers are ink pens

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.

Conclusions:

questions.question: Which of the following dietary components per gram provides the highest energy in humans?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Fats are the slowest source of energy but the most energy-efficient form of food.

 
 
• Each gram of fat supplies the body with about 9 calories, more than twice that supplied by proteins or carbohydrates.
 
• Because fats are such an efficient form of energy, the body stores any excess energy as fat.
 
• Fats form the most concentrated source of energy in our diet.
 
• 1 gram of fat yields 9.5 kcal of energy which is the highest among the food components.
 
• 1 gram of carbohydrates and proteins yield an almost similar amount of energy which is equal to 4 kcal.

• Proteins and most carbohydrates have about 17 kJ/g (4.1 kcal/g).

questions.question: At the same time A and B start moving towards each other from two different places, 240 km apart. The ratio of the speeds of A and B is 5 : 7, and the speed of B is 84 km/h. After how many minutes will A and B meet each other?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds **A : B = 5 : 7**

Given speed of **B = 84 km/h** ⇒ 7 units = 84 ⇒ 1 unit = 12 km/h

Total speed (Relative) = (5 + 7) units = 12 × 12 = **144 km/h**

Time = (Distance ÷ Relative Speed) × 60 = (240 ÷ 144) × 60 = **100 min**

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance = 240 km, Speed Ratio (A:B) = 5 : 7, Speed of B = 84 km/h.

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed; 1 hour = 60 minutes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e892a548e98792b7bc63895e0d3b3b4c6375c74f6ff34853cab5ac271e814439.png] 

⇒ Speed of **B** = 84 km/h

⇒ Ratio **A : B** = 5 : 7

⇒ Speed of **A** = (84 ÷ 7) × 5 = 12 × 5 = 60 km/h

⇒ **Relative Speed** (Opposite Direction) = Speed of A + Speed of B

⇒ Relative Speed = 60 + 84 = 144 km/h

⇒ **Time to meet** (in hours) = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 240 ÷ 144 = 5/3 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = (5 ÷ 3) × 60

⇒ Time = 5 × 20 = 100 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Meeting Time Formula

Time taken to meet = (Initial distance between them) ÷ (Relative Speed).</p
